key_insight: ZipMap introduces a stateful feed-forward architecture that converts quadratic cross-image cost into a linear-time process by maintaining and updating a compact scene map, enabling high-quality bidirectional 3D reconstruction with test-time adaptation.
problem_solved: Existing transformer-based 3D reconstruction methods scale quadratically with the number of input images, making them computationally and memory inefficient for large image collections; ZipMap addresses this scalability-quality tradeoff.
method: Stateful feed-forward model that maintains a compact, updatable scene representation (the 'ZipMap') across images so each new view incurs only constant additional cost.
Bidirectional reconstruction pipeline: sequentially integrates information from images while allowing refinement in both directions via the maintained state.
Test-time training/ adaptation applied on the maintained map to recover or exceed the reconstruction quality of heavy quadratic-cost methods.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable way to run high-quality 3D reconstruction on large photo collections or streaming inputs, cutting compute and memory costs while preserving or improving accuracy—useful for real-time systems and large-scale datasets.
visual_elements: Log–log plot comparing computational cost: quadratic (baseline transformers) vs linear (ZipMap) as number of images increases.
Pipeline diagram showing image stream → ZipMap state update → bidirectional refinement (with a test-time training loop overlay).
Side-by-side qualitative reconstructions: baseline quadratic model vs ZipMap on a large multi-view scene.
Icons/annotated callouts for speed (clock), memory efficiency (RAM chip), and reconstruction quality (3D mesh/point cloud).
paper_title: ZipMap: Linear-Time Stateful 3D Reconstruction with Test-Time Training
paper_authors: Haian Jin, Rundi Wu, Tianyuan Zhang, Ruiqi Gao, Jonathan T. Barron
